new_statements.quote: Der Acutus ´ deutet den dynamischen Akzent an. Meist fällt dieser auf die letzte Silbe und wird dann nicht besonders bezeichnet.
new_statements.translation: The acute ´ indicates the dynamic (stress) accent. Mostly it falls on the last syllable and is then not specially marked.
new_statements.locator: p. 546, section 'Lautlehre' (archive.org issue scan anthropos_may-august-1931_26_3-4, PDF page 222; page 2 of the 6-page extract)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote: opened (6-page extract; extracted text p. 2) and the page image. Printed p. 546, section 'Lautlehre', third paragraph reads exactly: "Der Acutus ´ deutet den dynamischen Akzent an. Meist fällt dieser auf die letzte Silbe und wird dann nicht besonders bezeichnet." Locator checked: extract p. 2 = issue-scan PDF p. 222 = printed p. 546 (headers "546 HERBERT BALDUS," and "Kaskihá-Vokabular. 545" on PDF p. 221 confirmed). Identity: p. 545 opens "Kaskihá nennt sich der Stamm der im nordöstlichen Chaco (Südamerika) lebenden Maskoi-Gruppe, der bei den Weißen und in der Literatur unter dem Namen Guaná bekannt ist. Da letzterer jedoch zu häufigen Verwechslungen mit dem gleichnamigen Arawakenst…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (Baldus's 'dynamischer Akzent') falls on the final syllable in most words; words with stress elsewhere are marked with an acute in the vocabulary. No rule is given for the non-final cases.
new_statements.exceptions: Implicitly many: 'meist' (mostly) final, and the vocabulary pp. 547-550 carries acute marks on a sizeable minority of forms, typically prefixed possessed nouns (scanned readings, unverified: héaxtik 'my eye', hémpedatik 'my eyelid', hémpik 'my finger', mopiépik 'fingernail'). Whether these reflect morphological (root-)stress or lexical exceptions is not analysed.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms from a 1928 wordlist elicited at Puerto Sastre from chief Ramón (and his wife); impressionistic transcription by an ethnologist, no instrumental or phrase-level data. Sister-language descriptions caution that Enlhet-Enenlhet prominence is complex: Van Gysel 2024 finds Sanapaná nouns most prominent on the final syllable in isolation but strongly affected by intonation; Elliott 2021 declines to state a single stress rule for Enxet Sur.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand statement is Baldus 1931, whose 'Kaskihá' is explicitly the Maskoi (Enlhet-Enenlhet) group of Puerto Sastre known to outsiders as Guaná (Baldus p. 545; Fabre 2005 sec. 4.1) — i.e. guan1268, NOT the homonymous Arawakan Guaná/Chané-Kinikinao of Brazil. Data elicited Aug 1928 from chief Ramón and his wife. No modern (Unruh & Kalisch / Van Gysel) statement on Guaná stress could be opened.

new_statements.quote: En todas las palabras guaná, la última sílaba es la acentuada. Por lo tanto no hace falta escribir un acento
new_statements.translation: In all Guaná words, the last syllable is the stressed one. Therefore there is no need to write an accent.
new_statements.citation: Unruh, Ernesto and Kalisch, Hannes (1999). Vana Peema. Nentenyey'a Nelhpaqmeesma Nempeema. Guía del Maestro Maskoy para el Aprendizaje del Idioma Guaná. Lecciones 1 a 16. Ya'alve-Saanga: Nengvaanemquescama Nempayvaam Enlhet. 82 pp.
new_statements.locator: p. 75, Anexo: Explicación Gramatical, sec. '3. La ortografía guaná' (PDF p. 39, right-hand page; verified on the page image because the text layer garbles capitals and 'ú')
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File present: (43 PDF pp., 2-up; Viewed the page image printed pp. 74-75): sec. '3. La ortografía guaná', last paragraph of p. 75 reads exactly "En todas las palabras guaná, la última sílaba es la acentuada. Por lo tanto no hace falta escribir un acento" (no final full stop on the page, as quoted). The text layer renders 'ú' as 'fl' and capitals as symbols, so the image check was necessary; the reader's caveat is right. Whole-book a full-text search for stress/accent acent/sílaba/tónic/entona/prosod finds only this statement plus the intonation remarks on questions (printed pp. 50-51, PDF p. 27: 'A veces, la pregunta solamente se marca a través de la entonación' / 'entonación es la melodía…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog rule (final) and as Baldus 1931 ('meist.. auf die letzte Silbe'); stronger than Baldus in admitting no exceptions. Refers to the Guaná spoken in the Maskoy communities of Machete Vayna, Castilla, Km 39, Km 40, Riacho Mosquito and Río Apa (Alto Paraguay).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the final syllable of every word; the orthography therefore writes no accent marks. The vocabulary (pp. 76-82) and the lesson dialogues carry no accents, consistent with this.
new_statements.exceptions: none ('todas las palabras'); the only other prosodic remark is that questions are sometimes marked by intonation alone (p. 50-51, 'entonación es la melodía de la frase entera')
new_statements.identity_note: Unruh & Kalisch 1999 describe the Guaná (vana peema) of the Maskoy communities of Machete Vayna, Castilla, Kilómetro 39, Kilómetro 40, Riacho Mosquito and Río Apa, Alto Paraguay, a revitalisation variety chosen because it was the only one of the five community languages still spoken; Baldus 1931 (already in the catalog) recorded 'Kaskihá' at Puerto Sastre in 1928, the same Enlhet-Enenlhet group. Van Gysel 2017 is primarily about Sanapaná (La Esperanza), with a short Guaná comparison section drawn entirely from Unruh & Kalisch 1999.

sources.citation: Elliott, John Alexander. 2021. A Grammar of Enxet Sur. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sister language only. Sec. 2.5.1 (pp. 115-118): Enxet Sur stress 'cannot be adequately summed up by a generalization like stress is typically on the penultimate syllable'; intensity favours the first syllable and pitch the second in CV.CVC nouns; earlier claims of penult stress (Powys 1929) called simplistic. Guaná is mentioned only for classification and pronominal-prefix morphology (citing Unruh & Kalisch 1999b: 74); no Guaná stress remark.
